what: Carrier tests of claims register v4 section 1.8 for every conditional target (TSV status 'conditional'): Rasero (24 rows), Buch (212), Mamat (28), Romero-Garcia (48). Pre-registered before the freeze; run under each target's gate by arcs/audit/src_register/carrier_test.py, which prints pass / fail and counts only.

rules.normalisation_dk: lower-case; strip; hemisphere read from a leading token (ctx-lh-, ctx_lh_, lh_, lh-, lh., lh , left-, left_, l_, l-) or a trailing token (_lh, -lh, _l, _left, ' (l)', ' left') or, if absent, from a separate column of the same table whose cells are all hemisphere tokens (l, r, lh, rh, left, right); the token removed; then every non-alphanumeric character removed; aliases: thalamus -> thalamusproper, accumbens -> accumbensarea (FreeSurfer 7 names). A name with no hemisphere matches nothing (reported as n_unlateralised).
rules.normalisation_dk308: as normalisation_dk (hemisphere token required); the remainder is compared with the annot name lower-cased (e.g. 'ctx-lh-bankssts_part1', 'lh_bankssts_part1', 'lh.bankssts_part1' -> L:bankssts_part1); non-alphanumerics other than '_' removed on both sides.
rules.normalisation_schaefer: lower-case; strip; a leading '17networks_' (or '17networks-') removed; '-', ' ' and '.' turned into '_'; compared with the CBIG name after the same steps (e.g. '17Networks_LH_VisCent_ExStr_1' -> lh_viscent_exstr_1). Where the target's 'index_labels' reading applies (Mamat), a table without names also qualifies through a column of integer parcel indices -- index i = the i-th parcel of the Schaefer 2018 400-parcel 17-network order file (labels_detail 'index') -- ONLY IF the carrier itself names that order file (index_labels.requires_order_file_named: its 17-network pattern found in the carrier's text -- any table cell, sheet or table name, or document / page text -- and no other Schaefer order file named); else index-only tables do not qualify (register v6 R9). Names are tried first and win a tie; an index table is subject to every other rule (all 400 indices present once, every value numeric).
rules.power_matching: a carrier row is a USABLE ROI for map M iff it has three numeric MNI coordinates -- in the row itself, or joined through its integer ROI id to coordinates given elsewhere in the carrier -- and a numeric value in M's column; an ROI id is NOT required (the sphere rule of register 1.7 uses the carrier's own coordinates, not an id list; register v5 section 1.11 item 8). Rows are keyed by their id where one is given, else by their coordinates; a key present twice with different values -> fail (duplicate labels). Power 2011 matching is a diagnostic only: an ROI is 'Power-matched' iff its coordinates lie within 2.0 mm (Euclidean) of the Power 2011 ROI of the same id, else of any Power 2011 ROI (then matched by coordinates); a row with numeric coordinates that matches no Power ROI is 'extra' (Buch's 277-ROI set exceeds Power's 264) and is usable. Coordinates: three columns headed x / y / z (optional 'mni', '(mm)'), or one column holding 'x, y, z' / '(x y z)' triples.
rules.numeric_parse: a value parses iff it is an int / float cell, or a string that after stripping and replacing U+2212 by '-' matches ^[+-]?(\d+(\.\d*)?|\.\d+)([eE][+-]?\d+)?$; the number must be finite. Empty cells, 'NA', 'n.s.', '-', '*'-suffixed or bracketed values do not parse. EVERY required label's value must parse.
rules.tables: every table of the carrier is searched: xlsx / xls sheets (openpyxl, values only), csv / tsv, docx w:tbl tables (XML, no macros), ipynb output tables (text/html <table>), PDF tables (pdfplumber page.extract_tables(), installed under the gate; untested here). A table's label column is the column whose cells match the most required labels; a hemisphere column is paired with it when its names carry no hemisphere.
rules.map_identification: a value column belongs to map M iff its header text (every non-numeric cell above the first label-matched row, joined) matches M's tier-1 pattern (map token AND object token); if no column of the carrier does, tier 2 (map token alone); if still none, a table whose sheet / table name matches M's map token and that holds exactly one numeric-for-all-matched-rows column. Exactly one column per map across the carrier at the tier used, else 'ambiguous' (fail) or 'no map column' (fail). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions.
rules.duplicates: a required label present twice in the chosen label column with different values -> fail (duplicate labels)
rules.output: pass / fail per map with a reason code and counts only; no label, header, value or file content is printed
rules.partial: partial or figure-only content does not qualify (register 1.8): a missing required label is a fail

source1_lists.what: the source-1 criterion (register 1.6; v6.1 Q1 made positive by v6.2 P1, keyed by cell id by P2, its checks confined by P6; v6.3 O1-O4 and O6; v6.4 N1-N4): a carrier list qualifies only if the carrier presents it as the set's membership used as input to the enrichment -- its own sheet name, table title, caption or its own (forward-filled) title carries input wording -- and no cell of its sheet (docx / pdf: its table and caption), other than the lists' own genes, carries statistics, result or map wording; where the paper prints a set size, the list length must equal it; otherwise the else branch applies
applies_to: Buch MOESM3 (every Buch enrichment and descriptor cell)
the R2 rows (RG-04, RG-V08, RG-V09, RG-N03 ... N07, BUCH-E-Trans-StructConstRibosome-S1 ... S4)

source1_lists.rule: (0) text: every heading is read after the name rule's normalisation (case, UK / US spelling, singular / plural) with '_' and '.' read as spaces (v6.3 O1 (b)); markers match at letter boundaries, so 'PLS1', 'core_enrichment', 'GSEA_results', 'SG1', 'top_genes', 'hit_gene', 'urg_list' are read. (1) candidates: (A) a column of gene symbols (symbol_pattern) below its title, or (B) a delimited list of >= 2 gene symbols in a row whose first cell names the set. A column's first data row is its first cell that is a gene symbol or a delimited symbol list and is followed (next filled cell below) by another such cell or by nothing (v6.3: a symbol-shaped header such as 'NES' over numbers is a title); a cell equal to a registered set name is a title, not data ('SYNGO'). A table's caption = its sheet name (xlsx) or file name (csv / txt), the paragraph just before it (docx) or the text line just above it (pdf), and its title rows (rows above its first data row with exactly one filled cell, in a table of >= 2 filled columns); a column's own title = its cells above ITS first data row (header rows forward-filled across merged cells; title rows excluded); for (B) the row's first cell is also part of the list's own title; the table's column titles = every column's cells in the header rows above the table's first data row. (2) naming: a heading names the set iff every phrase of one of the cell's name alternatives (cells) appears in it as whole words; (A) is named by its own title, by its own title and the caption together (at least one phrase in its own title; v6.3, for a table with one column per set under a caption naming the family, e.g. 'Top 500 cell-type-specific genes (Zhang 2014)' over 'Neuron' ...), or by the caption alone where the table has <= 2 titled columns; a heading naming another registered set of the target, or one of the target's rival names (rival_names: v6.3 O6), whose name contains the cell's names the more specific one ('Cytosolic ribosome' and 'Structural constituent of ribosome' are not 'Ribosome'). (3) refusals, after every phrase of the cell's own alternatives is removed wherever it appears (v6.3 O3) and 'top N' with N = the cell's printed size is exempt: result wording (result_markers) in the list's own title or the caption -> 'result list (result wording)'; statistics wording (statistics_headers, per heading part) in the list's own title, the caption or ANY column title of its table (v6.3 O1 (a)) -> 'result list (statistics wording)'; a name of one of the paper's maps, subgroups or cohorts (map_names: general and the cell's target) in its own title or the caption -> 'result list (the heading names a map, subgroup or cohort)'; no input wording (input_markers) in the caption or the list's own forward-filled title (v6.3 O2) -> 'not presented as input'; a column with non-symbol cells -> 'not a list of gene symbols'. (4) size: the cell's printed_size, else a size in the list's own heading ('n = N', '(N genes)', 'top N'), must equal the list's length. Exactly one qualifying list (identical duplicates merge) -> source 1; none, two or more distinct, or a size mismatch -> the else branch. (5) a family cell whose names come from the gated table (RG-03, RG-V06, RG-V07): one run per pathway with exactly one --name (the printed name as one phrase; a printed '[ _]Homo sapiens[ _]hsaNNNNN' suffix split off; several names for one run are refused, so no alternative accumulates across pathways; v6.3 O4); the table's other printed pathway names are passed as rival-only names (--rival; never alternatives; v6.4 N4). v6.4 (N1-N3) on top of (0)-(5): (6) SHEET-LEVEL REFUSAL (N1 (1)): if any cell of the list's sheet (xlsx; the whole csv / txt; for docx / pdf the whole table), other than the cells of the lists' own gene runs, or its caption carries statistics, result or map wording after the same reading (the phrases of the cell's own family removed, 'top N' = its printed size exempt), every list on that sheet is refused -> 'result list (statistics, result or map wording on the sheet)'; a cell that reads as ONE token counts only when the whole token equals a registered header (whole_tokens: fullmatch), a cell of several words by the phrase wording (statistics_headers, result_markers, map_names); the table-level and header-zone checks stay as a second layer. (7) a single-token cell is never data (never a gene of a list) if it is NA / NS / ND / NAN / N/A (na_like) or if, as read, the WHOLE token equals a registered statistics header, result marker or map name (whole_tokens; N1 (2) as refined in v6.4: not by substring or prefix, so P2RY12, P4HB, S100P, TOP1 or a pseudogene '...P1' are data) -- so 'NES' over 'NA', 'FDR' over 'NS', 'P' over 'NS', 'PLS1', 'CORE' or 'SG1' as titles stay titles; the cost, counted (non_data_cost): the approved HGNC symbols equal to a registered token, which fall into a list's title when they are its first gene(s), so that list is refused as a whole. (8) naming (N2): own title and caption together name a set only for a family with caption_phrases (the Zhang cells: the phrases the caption supplies must be 'zhang' or 'top 500'); a cell with own_title_only (RG-15, RG-V23) is named only by its own title. (9) 'weighted gene co-expression' is not the 'weight' marker (N3). v6.5: (10) CORROBORATION (the orchestrator's decision after five review rounds, v6.0 -> v6.4, showed that the text criterion alone could not exclude result lists; the text criterion stays as a first filter): the one list the text criterion admits is source 1 only if corroborated -- (a) mode 'external' / 'external_under_gate': Jaccard(the list's HGNC genes in the cell's class universe, the external set's HGNC genes in that universe) >= corroboration.threshold (.80); the external set is the pinned register_sets set (external; v6.6 B1: pinned by set id and sha256) or, for the Romero-Garcia KEGG families, the pathway the engine builds by the recipe (v6.6 B1; v6.5's --external withdrawn); (b) mode 'printed_size': the list's length equals the printed size; (c) mode 'none': never corroborated -> the else branch, 'not auditable (S undefined: source 1 uncorroborated)'. A leading-edge, overlap, hit or core-enrichment list is a strict subset of its set, so it fails (a) and (b) by construction. (11) M1: a cell of words separated by spaces is a gene list only if no word is NA-like or a registered whole token, the cell carries no statistics / result / map phrase, it is not a generic title (generic_titles), and it does not stand directly over a column of single symbols (then it is that column's title); M2: dashes (ASCII and Unicode) read as spaces, 'leading-edge' in every form; M3: a single token that is not gene-symbol-shaped is also split on punctuation and camelCase and each piece matched against the whole-token registry (pieces 't', 'es', 'or', 'se' excepted); M4: NA-like cells are dropped from a list's members. v6.6 (the orchestrator under the operator's standing delegation, 2026-09-27; the v6.5 re-check's B1, B2, C1-C3, C6): (12) B1 -- every comparator is pinned per cell (corroboration.set_id with the committed per-set JSON's sha256 and its members' sha256, or, for the Romero-Garcia KEGG families, the recipe with its libraries' sha256); the engine reads the comparator only from the committed register_sets folder, refuses a file whose set id, class or either sha256 differs, records the set id and hashes it used, and sends every read / parse / mismatch error to the else branch with its reason; no comparator file is accepted from outside (--external withdrawn). (13) B2 -- Buch's and Pagani's comparators are built before the freeze (register 1.6 resolution rule); a set the rule cannot build is 'not auditable (S undefined: comparator not buildable pre-freeze)' and its cells take mode none. (14) C1 -- the printed-size check counts DISTINCT APPROVED HGNC symbols of the list (the S-build's HGNC rule: approved, previous, alias), not rows. (15) C2 -- an approved, previous or alias HGNC symbol is never split into pieces (M3's split applies to other tokens only); a whole token equal to a registered header stays never-data (cost counted: non_data_cost). (16) C3 -- a generic title (generic_titles) is a title before the symbol test ('GENES', 'SYMBOL' over a list are its title, not its first gene). (17) C6 -- statistics wording also as a whole cell: the single tokens 'r', 't', 'corr', 'correlation' (whole_tokens) and the cells 't value' / 't-value' and 'OR (95% CI)' (whole_cells: the whole cell, as read, must match; no gene symbol is affected). v6.7: (18) a registered SECONDARY VIEW, 'near-miss comparator' (cells[<id>].corroboration_views.near_miss, run with source1 --view near_miss): for the Buch and Pagani cells whose comparator is not buildable, a comparator from a near-miss source (not the cited reference) or reached by a declared name normalisation (v6.8: or the cited source's list reached through a name bridge from a reference not cited for the set -- asdM12; v6.9: or a list reached by a semantic reading of a column note, not its title -- ASD rare de novo, Sanders 2019's ASD65; v6.10: the label names these 'note reading', PAG-C9 / C10's modules read from Gandal 2022's text among them); the view never changes the primary run. v6.7 N3: the class universes and the HGNC table are pinned by sha256 (corroboration.universe_genes_sha256, hgnc_table), asserted by the engine inside the try / except that sends every read / parse / pin mismatch to the else branch
